    Supervised GMM vs. EM vs. CEM¶

    This notebook compares three ways of fitting a GaussianMixture on the same synthetic data:

    • EM: standard soft-assignment fitting, no label information.
    • CEM: Classification EM — hard assignment via argmax(resp) each iteration, no label information.
    • Supervised: fit(X, labels=y) — the assignment comes from the true label instead of argmax(resp), converging in a single M-step (see the "Supervised Fitting" section of the user guide, and docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-10-supervised-gmm-design.md for the literature this is grounded in: Celeux & Govaert 1992, McLachlan & Peel 2000, Fraley & Raftery 2002).

    The data reuses all 4 Gaussian components from notebooks/01_gmm.ipynb (same centers/covariances/sample counts), but two of them share one label -- so there are only 3 classes even though there are 4 physical blobs. That's deliberate: EM/CEM don't see labels, so with n_components=3 they're free to find whichever 3-way split fits the data best (which turns out not to match the label grouping), while the supervised fit is bound by the label and has to force a single Gaussian across two blobs it's told belong together. This is what makes the three methods diverge visibly instead of agreeing trivially.

    In [1]:
    Copied! 
    import torch
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import time

import os
os.chdir('../')

import tgmm
import importlib
importlib.reload(tgmm)

from tgmm import (
    GaussianMixture, plot_gmm, dynamic_figsize, generate_gmm_data,
    gmm_proxy, confidence_ellipse_std_devs, ClusteringMetrics,
)

device = 'cuda' if torch.cuda.is_available() else 'cpu'
random_state = 42
np.random.seed(random_state)
torch.manual_seed(random_state)
print('Using device:', device)
    import torch import numpy as np import matplotlib.pyplot as plt import time import os os.chdir('../') import tgmm import importlib importlib.reload(tgmm) from tgmm import ( GaussianMixture, plot_gmm, dynamic_figsize, generate_gmm_data, gmm_proxy, confidence_ellipse_std_devs, ClusteringMetrics, ) device = 'cuda' if torch.cuda.is_available() else 'cpu' random_state = 42 np.random.seed(random_state) torch.manual_seed(random_state) print('Using device:', device)
    Using device: cpu

    Data: 4 Gaussians from 01_gmm.ipynb, 2 sharing one label¶

    Same 4 centers/covariances/sample counts as notebooks/01_gmm.ipynb. The two spatially farthest-apart components -- (2, -2) and (2, 2), distance 4.0 -- share Class 2; (0, 2) and (0, 0) keep their own labels. The closest pair, (0, 2) and (0, 0) (distance 2.0), is exactly what an unsupervised 3-component fit tends to merge instead -- the opposite of the label grouping.

    In [2]:
    Copied! 
    centers = [
    np.array([0, 2]),
    np.array([0, 0]),
    np.array([2, -2]),
    np.array([2, 2]),
]
covs = [
    1.0 * np.eye(2),                    # spherical covariance
    np.array([[2, 0], [0, 0.5]]),       # diagonal covariance
    0.5 * np.eye(2),                    # spherical covariance, fewer points
    np.array([[0.2, 0.5], [0.5, 2]]),   # full covariance
]
n_samples = [800, 1000, 200, 1000]

# Components 2 and 3 (the two farthest apart, distance 4.0) share one
# label -- physical_to_label[i] is the class label for physical blob i.
physical_to_label = torch.tensor([0, 1, 2, 2])
n_components = 3
legend_labels = [f'Class {i}' for i in range(n_components)]

X_tensor, y_physical = generate_gmm_data(centers, covs, n_samples, device=device, random_state=random_state)
y_tensor = physical_to_label.to(y_physical.device)[y_physical]
X = X_tensor.cpu().numpy()
y_true = y_tensor.cpu().numpy()
    centers = [ np.array([0, 2]), np.array([0, 0]), np.array([2, -2]), np.array([2, 2]), ] covs = [ 1.0 * np.eye(2), # spherical covariance np.array([[2, 0], [0, 0.5]]), # diagonal covariance 0.5 * np.eye(2), # spherical covariance, fewer points np.array([[0.2, 0.5], [0.5, 2]]), # full covariance ] n_samples = [800, 1000, 200, 1000] # Components 2 and 3 (the two farthest apart, distance 4.0) share one # label -- physical_to_label[i] is the class label for physical blob i. physical_to_label = torch.tensor([0, 1, 2, 2]) n_components = 3 legend_labels = [f'Class {i}' for i in range(n_components)] X_tensor, y_physical = generate_gmm_data(centers, covs, n_samples, device=device, random_state=random_state) y_tensor = physical_to_label.to(y_physical.device)[y_physical] X = X_tensor.cpu().numpy() y_true = y_tensor.cpu().numpy()

    Fitting all three models¶

    EM and CEM don't see y_tensor at all; only the supervised fit does.

    In [3]:
    Copied! 
    gmm_em = GaussianMixture(n_components=n_components, random_state=random_state)
t0 = time.time()
gmm_em.fit(X_tensor)
time_em = time.time() - t0

gmm_cem = GaussianMixture(n_components=n_components, random_state=random_state, cem=True)
t0 = time.time()
gmm_cem.fit(X_tensor)
time_cem = time.time() - t0

gmm_sup = GaussianMixture(n_components=n_components)
t0 = time.time()
gmm_sup.fit(X_tensor, labels=y_tensor)
time_sup = time.time() - t0

print(f"EM:         iters={gmm_em.n_iter_:4d}  converged={gmm_em.converged_}  time={time_em:.4f}s  mean log-lik={gmm_em.score(X_tensor):.4f}")
print(f"CEM:        iters={gmm_cem.n_iter_:4d}  converged={gmm_cem.converged_}  time={time_cem:.4f}s  mean log-lik={gmm_cem.score(X_tensor):.4f}")
print(f"Supervised: iters={gmm_sup.n_iter_:4d}  converged={gmm_sup.converged_}  time={time_sup:.4f}s  mean log-lik={gmm_sup.score(X_tensor):.4f}")
print(f"\nSupervised gmm.classes_: {gmm_sup.classes_.cpu().tolist()}")
    gmm_em = GaussianMixture(n_components=n_components, random_state=random_state) t0 = time.time() gmm_em.fit(X_tensor) time_em = time.time() - t0 gmm_cem = GaussianMixture(n_components=n_components, random_state=random_state, cem=True) t0 = time.time() gmm_cem.fit(X_tensor) time_cem = time.time() - t0 gmm_sup = GaussianMixture(n_components=n_components) t0 = time.time() gmm_sup.fit(X_tensor, labels=y_tensor) time_sup = time.time() - t0 print(f"EM: iters={gmm_em.n_iter_:4d} converged={gmm_em.converged_} time={time_em:.4f}s mean log-lik={gmm_em.score(X_tensor):.4f}") print(f"CEM: iters={gmm_cem.n_iter_:4d} converged={gmm_cem.converged_} time={time_cem:.4f}s mean log-lik={gmm_cem.score(X_tensor):.4f}") print(f"Supervised: iters={gmm_sup.n_iter_:4d} converged={gmm_sup.converged_} time={time_sup:.4f}s mean log-lik={gmm_sup.score(X_tensor):.4f}") print(f"\nSupervised gmm.classes_: {gmm_sup.classes_.cpu().tolist()}")

    Visual comparison¶

    2x2 grid: true classes, EM, CEM, supervised. All four panels use the same 3 blue shades for Class 0/1/2, drawn entirely through plot_gmm -- no hand-rolled matplotlib. The "True Classes" panel uses gmm_proxy to feed the 4 true generating Gaussians (not a fitted model) into plot_gmm, with cluster_colors repeating Class 2's blue for the two merged physical components. EM/CEM component indices are arbitrary, so match_labels_to_true Hungarian-matches them to the true labels for both point and ellipse coloring; show_incorrect_predictions then colors correct points by their matched cluster color and incorrect ones red -- so misclassifications are directly visible, concentrated where the forced 3-way split disagrees with the (arbitrary) label grouping. The supervised fit needs no matching, since its component index already is the label (classes_ == [0, 1, 2]). Ellipses are 95% confidence regions via confidence_ellipse_std_devs(0.95) (Mahalanobis radius sqrt(chi2.ppf(0.95, df=2)), not "2 standard deviations" -- that's a 1D interval, not a 2D confidence region), and markers show each component's mean.

    In [4]:
    Copied! 
    from matplotlib.patches import Patch
from matplotlib.lines import Line2D

BLUE_SHADES = ['#9ecae1', '#4292c6', '#08519c']  # Class 0, 1, 2
WRONG_COLOR = '#d62728'                          # incorrect predictions (EM/CEM only)
CONF_95 = confidence_ellipse_std_devs(0.95)      # chi2-based 95% CI multiplier, not "2 std devs"

ellipse_kwargs = dict(show_ellipses=True, ellipse_std_devs=CONF_95, ellipse_fill=True, ellipse_alpha=0.15)
mean_kwargs = dict(show_means=True, mean_color='black', mean_size=60)

fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 2, figsize=dynamic_figsize(2, 2))
fig.suptitle('True labels vs. EM vs. CEM vs. Supervised')

# True classes: the 4 physical Gaussians via gmm_proxy (a stand-in `gmm=`
# object built from the raw generating parameters, not a fitted model),
# colored by the label each was folded into -- physical components 2 and 3
# both get Class 2's blue.
true_proxy = gmm_proxy(
    means=np.stack(centers), covariances=np.stack(covs),
    covariance_type='full', predicted_labels=y_physical,
)
true_cluster_colors = [BLUE_SHADES[label] for label in physical_to_label.tolist()]
plot_gmm(X=X, gmm=true_proxy, ax=axes[0, 0], title='True Classes',
         color_by_cluster=True, cluster_colors=true_cluster_colors,
         point_size=8, legend=False, **ellipse_kwargs, **mean_kwargs)

# EM / CEM: match_labels_to_true Hungarian-matches the arbitrary component
# indices to true labels for both point and ellipse coloring;
# show_incorrect_predictions colors correct points by their matched cluster
# color and incorrect ones in WRONG_COLOR.
plot_gmm(X=X, gmm=gmm_em, ax=axes[0, 1], title=f'EM\n({gmm_em.n_iter_} iters)',
         color_by_cluster=True, true_labels=y_true, match_labels_to_true=True,
         cluster_colors=BLUE_SHADES, show_incorrect_predictions=True, incorrect_color=WRONG_COLOR,
         point_size=8, legend=False, **ellipse_kwargs, **mean_kwargs)

plot_gmm(X=X, gmm=gmm_cem, ax=axes[1, 0], title=f'CEM\n({gmm_cem.n_iter_} iters)',
         color_by_cluster=True, true_labels=y_true, match_labels_to_true=True,
         cluster_colors=BLUE_SHADES, show_incorrect_predictions=True, incorrect_color=WRONG_COLOR,
         point_size=8, legend=False, **ellipse_kwargs, **mean_kwargs)

# Supervised: component index already is the label (classes_ == [0, 1, 2]),
# no Hungarian matching needed. Not correctness-colored (only EM/CEM get the
# red/blue treatment) -- points are colored by gmm_sup's own predict(),
# which by construction of the supervised fit matches the given label
# almost everywhere.
plot_gmm(X=X, gmm=gmm_sup, ax=axes[1, 1], title='Supervised\n(1 iter)',
         color_by_cluster=True, cluster_colors=BLUE_SHADES,
         point_size=8, legend=False, **ellipse_kwargs, **mean_kwargs)

legend_handles = (
    [Patch(facecolor=BLUE_SHADES[i], edgecolor='none', label=f'Class {i}') for i in range(n_components)]
    + [Patch(facecolor=WRONG_COLOR, edgecolor='none', label='Incorrect (EM/CEM)'),
       Line2D([0], [0], marker='h', color='w', markerfacecolor='black', markersize=9, label='Component mean'),
       Line2D([0], [0], color='gray', linestyle='dotted', linewidth=2, label='95% confidence region')]
)
fig.legend(handles=legend_handles, loc='center left', bbox_to_anchor=(1.0, 0.5), fontsize='small')

plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
